summary.one_liner: A research implementation of Suspicion Agent, a GPT-4 agent that uses theory-of-mind reasoning to play imperfect-information card games against baseline agents.
summary.what_it_does: The repository is the code accompanying the paper "Suspicion Agent: Playing Imperfect Information Games with Theory of Mind Aware GPT-4". It provides a script, main_vs_baseline.py, that runs a GPT-4-driven agent against baseline rule-based agents. The baselines selectable through the --rule_model flag are cfr, nfsp, dqn, and dmc. A --user flag and a --verbose_print flag control interactive play and detailed output. The README also links a project demo and game data replay, though it does not describe those in text. The README says the code is based on SkyAGI and credits its authors. The Method and Sample Output sections are empty in the README.
use_cases: research on theory-of-mind reasoning in LLM game agents
benchmarking GPT-4 against CFR, NFSP, DQN, or DMC baselines
playing imperfect-information card games against an LLM agent
replaying recorded game data from agent matches
reproducing results from the Suspicion-Agent paper
how_to_run: Set up the OpenAI key following OPENAI_KEY
notable: Theory-of-mind aware prompting so the GPT-4 agent reasons about opponents' hidden information
Selectable baseline opponents: CFR, NFSP, DQN, and DMC
Interactive user mode and verbose output for watching agent decisions
Accompanies an arXiv paper (2309.17277) and includes a BibTeX citation
caveats: Requires an OpenAI API key with GPT-4 access, so running it costs money per API call
The README gives only a short install and run section and leaves Method and Sample Output empty
The README does not state a license
